title: Adaptive tier routing: region-aware demotion and quota-debt smoothing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Customers across free/paid/enterprise tiers experience sharp failures when token quotas or regional capacity are exhausted. Current behavior is mostly hard-reject or blunt fallback to a single low-cost model which leads to poor UX (surges of 429s) or quality cliffs for paid customers. We need a more graceful, accountable system that preserves enterprise SLOs while allowing free/paid traffic to continue at degraded quality when appropriate.

Goal:
Implement an adaptive tier routing controller that: 1) selects region-aware fallbacks and model-variant demotions rather than hard-rejects; 2) maintains a per-tenant "quota-debt" account that allows controlled temporary overuse with automated recovery smoothing; and 3) exposes telemetry and controls in Console so product and ops can understand tradeoffs.

Design summary:
- Admission controller keeps per-tenant sliding-window consumption + an elastic debt balance. When budget is exhausted, instead of immediate reject, the controller: 1) attempts a local-region variant demotion (e.g., llama-2-13b-quant -> llama-2-7b-quant) if permitted by tenant policy; 2) if local region capacity is constrained, attempts cross-region spillback to a pre-warmed secondary pool in a low-cost region; 3) if demotion/spillback not allowed or unavailable, apply soft-throttle (rate-limited backlog) with clear 429 gradients and observability.
- Debt model: tenants accrue a temporary debt token allowance (configurable per-plan) that decays on a configurable schedule (linear or exponential) and can be repaid via normal usage reductions or explicit billing reconciliations for commercial customers. Debt increases admission score but imposes progressive rate limits if debt crosses thresholds.
- Model-variant selection uses a priority matrix: [enterprise-allowed-variants] > [paid-allowed-variants] > [free-allowed-variants]. The router consults tenant policy before demoting. Fallback model performance/cost metadata is used to compute expected latency/quality delta.
- Telemetry: new metrics: tenant.debt_balance, tenant.debt_rate, fallback.count, fallback.path (region->variant), fallback.latency_delta. Console panels and per-route traces will show debt accrual events and predicted recovery windows.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement controller core, debt accounting, variant priority matrix, and basic region spillback rules. Add unit tests and integration tests.
- Phase 2: rollout canary to <5% of free traffic and 1% paid; gather metrics, tune decay windows, add cost-control knobs.
- Phase 3: full rollout with Console controls, billing hooks for enterprise reconciliations, and SLO guardrails.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Additional routing complexity increases request path decision time; mitigate via caching of decision outcomes for short TTLs and precomputed variant lists per-tenant.
- Cross-region spillback increases P99 latency for affected requests; only allowed when tenant policy permits or for free-tier best-effort.
- Debt model introduces billing reconciliation complexity for enterprise customers; product will own policy and billing integration.

Operational considerations:
- Feature flag gated rollout: runtime.feature_flags.tier_debt_router
- Default conservative per-plan debt: free=2000 tokens, paid=10000 tokens, enterprise=50000 tokens (configurable)
- SLO target: no more than 5% of enterprise requests experience demotion in steady state; paid <=10%; free best-effort.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller correctly routes to an allowed fallback variant according to tenant policy when primary capacity or quota is exhausted
Per-tenant debt account correctly accrues and decays; debt_balance exposed in metrics and matches expected calculations in unit tests
Cross-region spillback only occurs when configured and logs fallback.path with region and variant details
End-to-end tests simulate burst over-usage and verify no silent hard-rejects for paid/enterprise when demotion paths exist
Console shows debt metrics and a per-tenant predicted recovery window within 5% of computed value
